_readme: Real documents from real suppliers, sent by the client SME (AJ Conner) 2026-09-16 for wizard-config testing. Ground truth was written from the page text, not read back out of an extraction. See README.md.

sets.1: the COMPREHENSIVE set — one supplier who assembles a full clean packet (packet-fdlw-2026, 36 pages, 25 documents)
sets.2: the MESSIER set — four unrelated specification sheets from three suppliers, three different templates
sets.3: NOT YET ARRIVED — Medosweet's own packet plus AJ's manual

_provenance.why_real_pdfs_are_committed: The doctype-corpus and spec-corpus PDFs are gitignored because they are BUILD OUTPUT rebuilt from html/ by bin/render-*-corpus. These are not: a real supplier PDF has no source to rebuild from, so the PDF IS the source and is tracked. 2.1 MB for five files.

_document_type_expected_none_why: Eighteen of the packet's twenty-six parts have no matching type in the FSQA starter pack, and for those the CORRECT classifier answer is "none" — which parks the item for a human instead of forcing it onto the nearest name. The synthetic corpus never needed to say that, because every fixture there was written to match a type in the pack. `document_type_expected_none: true` says it. A document may carry BOTH that flag and a `document_type_accept` list, and then either answer counts: that combination is used exactly twice, where the pack has an adjacent-but-not-equal type and the disagreement is worth recording rather than resolving.
_key_groups_moved: `shelf_life` and `document_number` were defined HERE while neither was a field the extractor had — they were the watch lists proving the answers went nowhere. Both became canonical fields on 2026-09-17, so their key groups moved to ../doctype-corpus/corpus.json, which this file extends: one definition, shared by both corpora, instead of two that can drift.

documents.type: Supplier facility packet (25 documents in one PDF)
documents.document_type_note: THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ENTRY. 36 pages, 25 separately-dated documents, one upload. The classifier reads CLASSIFIER_TEXT_BUDGET = 3000 characters, which on this file is the cover letter and the table of contents and the first sentence of the Letter of Guarantee. Any confident single answer is wrong, because no single answer exists: whichever type it lands on becomes the type of all 25, and whichever date it lands on becomes the renewal date of all 25. Unresolved is the only correct answer until the packet is split.
pdf_text_must_contain: 2026 SUPPLIER INFORMATION FOR SAVENCIA CHEESE FLEUR DE

fields.name: supplier_name
accept: Savencia Cheese Fleur de Lait West
fields.why: the one field a packet CAN answer — every document in it is from the same supplier

fields.name: document_expires_on
fields.why: FOUR different real expiry dates live inside this file — SQF 2026-04-23, both OU kosher letters 2026-06-30, the alouette IFANCA halal 2026-10-31, the FDA registration 2026-12-31 — and none of them is the packet's. Picking any one silently sets the renewal date for the other 24 documents

fields.name: effective_date
fields.why: twenty of the twenty-five documents are dated January 2, 2026; the PDF itself was produced 2026-01-13, which is accepted as the same event

fields.name: certificate_number
fields.why: a packet has no certificate number; three real ones and two USDA plant numbers are inside it

documents.note: Page 36 is blank. Pages 6 and 13-16 are inserted certificate IMAGES with no text layer — in the whole-file text layer they contribute only the "C2" banner and a page number, so five of the packet's most renewal-relevant documents are invisible to a text-layer read of the whole file.

documents.type: 3rd Party Audit Certificate (SQF, issued by NSF)
documents.toc_label: 4. Global Standard for Food Safety Certificate | Page 6
documents.document_type_note: The INDEX CALLS IT SOMETHING IT IS NOT. "Global Standard for Food Safety" is BRCGS's product name; the certificate on the page is SQF (SQF Food Safety Code: Food Manufacturing, SQF Quality Code, Edition 9) issued by NSF Certification, LLC. A tenant that trusted the index would file a BRCGS certificate it does not hold. Both audit types in the starter pack are accepted because Certificate-vs-Report is the same fine distinction the synthetic corpus leaves standing.

fields.name: document_expires_on
fields.why: THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS. The alouette IFANCA certificate on the next page prints "valid until October 31, 2026"; THIS one, from the same certifier on the same day, prints no validity line at all. A reviewer skimming two near-identical certificates will assume both expire together. Ground truth is null — the page does not say — and October 31 2026 borrowed from the sibling page is an invention, because it is nowhere in THIS page's text

fields.name: plant_number
fields.why: "Plant code | 53-02". "#33-19" at the top of the letterhead is the document's own form number and is the decoy. It is deliberately NOT graded as document_number: the manifest asserts what it is from its position alone, the page never labels it, and a ground truth that rests on our own reading of an unlabelled number would be marking the model against a guess. An answer of "33-19" under document_number therefore costs nothing here, and is not credited either

documents.note: FOUR micro limits, NO UNITS, and TWO SCOPES — "Fresh" and "48 Hr Stress" — for the same two analytes. This is the hardest of the four for shared/specCheck.ts: a unitless limit and a scope that is a test condition rather than a product. It is the reason spec_limits_printed here is a description of the page, not an importable config.
